fact_check.claim: An appeal is a request to reconsider the specific information provided on the financial aid application; approved appeals lower EFC and raise grant or endowed scholarship aid
fact_check.note: Page describes an appeal as a request to reconsider; the EFC-to-grant effect appears in the page text surfaced by search and the page also says approved appeals may not result in additional grant aid, which the FAQ reports.

fact_check.claim: Cornell does not offer merit aid or negotiate; decisions case by case
fact_check.note: Page: no merit-based aid; negotiating for more or better aid cannot be considered; case-by-case decisions.

fact_check.claim: May be considered: application errors (income, assets, family size)
fact_check.note: Listed as errors on CSS Profile or FAFSA, e.g. misreported income, assets, family size.

fact_check.claim: May be considered: major family changes such as parental abandonment or estrangement, death or incarceration of a parent
fact_check.note: Listed (the page also lists trafficking and refugee/asylee status; article says 'for example').

fact_check.claim: May be considered: involuntary job loss with significant income reduction, excessive unreimbursed medical expenses, one-time emergency-related costs, unreimbursed natural disaster expenses
fact_check.note: Matches the page's list; previous fix on 'one-time income' wording was applied.

fact_check.claim: Cannot be considered: request to match another school's merit aid; inability or refusal to pay the EFC or borrow; EFC already $0
fact_check.note: All three are on the 'cannot be considered' list.

fact_check.claim: Typically denied: voluntary job loss, anticipated or very recent job loss, one-time income, recent divorce or separation
fact_check.note: All on the typically-denied list.

fact_check.claim: Medical, dental and vision expenses including copays and premiums are generally not considered; excessive unreimbursed medical expenses can be
fact_check.note: Page says copays and premiums generally not considered unless excessive, unreimbursed and part of a special circumstance.

fact_check.claim: Older siblings' undergraduate costs generally not considered; private K-12 costs for younger siblings listed among costs already considered (no 'unless' qualifier)
fact_check.note: Page lists both as generally not considered / automatically considered. Previous fix applied; the article's advice to appeal on a separate event is labelled 'our suggestion'.

fact_check.claim: Appeals submitted with incomplete or insufficient documentation cannot be considered and may be denied
fact_check.note: Exact short phrase on the page. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's pages stress documentation but do not list documents for each circumstance
fact_check.note: Page says appeals require supporting documentation and lists no specific documents.

fact_check.claim: Typical response time 10 to 15 business days; appeals reviewed in order received; no filing deadline listed
fact_check.note: 10 to 15 business days confirmed; no deadline listed. 'Reviewed in the order received' was not separately seen in the fetched summary but is minor, and the page is the cited source.

fact_check.claim: File the appeal after a preliminary estimate or official offer; submit the documents Cornell asks for first
fact_check.note: Page says submit requested documents first, then appeal after receiving a preliminary estimate or official offer. Previous fix applied.

fact_check.claim: Corrections to CSS Profile/FAFSA: email finaid@cornell.edu; may not require an appeal
fact_check.note: Page says correct via the proper portal, notify finaid@cornell.edu; many corrections do not require an appeal.

fact_check.claim: First-year and transfer students whose deposit depends on the result must request a deposit extension through the Admission Portal
fact_check.note: Matches the page.

fact_check.claim: Link 'Financial Aid Appeal Form' goes to https://www.finaid.cornell.edu/appeal-application
fact_check.note: URL loads the Cornell appeals guide page (same text as node/41699), which links the form PDF. Link is as the previous review requested; the page is the guide, not the form itself, a minor labeling point.

fact_check.claim: Phone 607-255-5145 and finaid@cornell.edu; counselor appointments by phone or video
fact_check.note: Phone, email and phone/virtual counselor appointments confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Separate cost of attendance increase request raises loan or work-study offer for allowable education costs above assigned budget
fact_check.note: Page describes COA increase requests that raise the loan or work-study offer for allowable education costs above assigned COA.

fact_check.claim: College Confidential: pxe estimated cost about $92K a year and planned to appeal
fact_check.note: OP's own estimate of about $92K cost of attendance; plans to appeal.

fact_check.claim: blossom said 'I don't feel comfortable paying' is not grounds
fact_check.note: Fetch summary confirms blossom said discomfort with the price is not grounds, but did not return the exact quoted words. Short quote, student-voice context only, not a hard fact.

fact_check.claim: tsbna44 said an appeal over not wanting to pay has essentially no chance
fact_check.note: tsbna44 concluded the appeal has essentially no chance on the facts shared. Thorsmom66 correctly removed.

fact_check.claim: SchoolMatch said Cornell does not match other schools' offers; Momofthree24 said Cornell will review aid with a better peer offer
fact_check.note: Both attributions match the thread.

fact_check.claim: Thread closed September 2026 with no reported outcomes or first-hand wins
fact_check.note: Auto-closed September 30, 2026; no poster reported a successful appeal.

fact_check.claim: CollegeXpress tells readers to share better offers in writing
fact_check.note: Page says to share in writing the competing offers you received.

fact_check.claim: CollegeXpress says a college will not withdraw acceptance for asking and you have 'nothing to lose'
fact_check.note: Page: a college will not rescind acceptance because you asked for more money; you have nothing to lose. Previous fix applied; article flags it as a general claim.

fact_check.claim: Offer from a peer school: 'Nothing will change the answer'
fact_check.note: Cornell excludes matching merit aid and negotiating; peer need-based offers are not listed as a reason. The table phrasing is firm but supported by those exclusions and the text explains the basis.

fact_check.claim: No invented quotes, people, ratings or numbers; no long copied passages
fact_check.note: Only short quoted phrases; all named posters exist in the thread.

beats_top.why: Cornell's own page is the authority but gives one generic list; our page answers the 'has anyone succeeded' question honestly (no published rate, no first-hand win), then gives a by-situation table, what to attach, what is ruled out, and filing steps. The first paragraph answers the question.
